title: Risk management: identification and mitigation in electrical installations
excerpt: Learn how to prevent risks in electrical installations through simple steps.

blocks.text: Effective risk management is essential in the field of electrical installations. Identifying and mitigating potential hazards is crucial to ensuring worker safety and the smooth operation of electrical systems. Here are some key strategies for risk management:
Initial risk assessment
Before any work, it is essential to carry out a detailed risk assessment. Identifying potential hazards, assessing their severity and likelihood of occurrence is the critical first step.
Regulatory compliance
Ensuring that all installations comply with local and international regulations is key. The regulations provide specific guidelines for electrical safety.
Use of appropriate equipment
Ensure that equipment and tools suitable for the task is essential. Defective or inappropriate equipment can significantly increase the risk of accidents.
Training and awareness
Continuous training of staff on the risks associated with electrical installations and best safety practices is crucial. A well-informed team is better able to identify and address risk situations.
Preventive maintenance
Implementing preventive maintenance programs for electrical equipment and systems helps prevent failures and reduces the risk of accidents. Early detection of problems can avoid dangerous situations.
Emergency plans
Developing and practicing emergency plans specific to electrical situations is vital. All workers must know the procedures to follow in the event of an emergency.
Continuous monitoring of risks in electrical installations
Risk management is a dynamic process. It is essential to continually monitor electrical installations to identify changes in conditions and adjust mitigation strategies as necessary.
Sources
NFPA 70E: Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace .
OSHA Electrical Safety Standards (29 CFR 1910 Subpart S) .

Implementing these strategies in electrical risk management helps create a safer work environment and protects both workers and facilities. Proactive identification and mitigation of risks are fundamental steps towards excellence in electrical safety.

title: Installing switches: tutorial for beginner electricians
excerpt: Learn how to install home switches step by step. Install a switch like a pro.

blocks.text: Installing electrical switches is a basic, but crucial task for any electrician, whether beginner or experienced. In this detailed tutorial, we will explore the fundamental steps to carry out this task safely and efficiently.
Step 1: Preparation and Safety

Before starting any electrical work, it is essential to take security measures . Be sure to disconnect the main power source and use personal protective equipment, including gloves and safety glasses. Safety is the number one priority in any electrical project.
Source: "Electrical Safety Regulations for Workers" - OSHA.
Step 2: Switch Identification

Each switch has a specific purpose, whether for lights, outlets, or other devices. Before you begin, identify the switch you plan to replace and note its function. This will make installing the new switch easier.
Source: "Practical Guide to Switch Identification" - National Electrical Code (NEC).
Step 3: Disconnect Power

Once the switch is identified, turn off the power at the breaker box. This can be achieved by turning off the corresponding key on the center panel. Use a test lamp to ensure the power is completely off before continuing.
Source: "Safe Procedures for Power Disconnection" - NFPA 70E.
Step 4: Removal of the old switch
Use a screwdriver to remove the old switch plate and unscrew the connected wires. Be sure to remember the location of each wire for proper installation of the new switch.
Source: "Tools and Techniques for Switch Removal" - Electrical Safety Foundation International (ESFI).
Step 5 – Preparing the New Switch

Before connecting the new switch, verify that it is compatible with your electrical system and complies with local regulations. Prepare the cables by carefully stripping them and making sure they are in good condition.
Source: "Specifications and Standards for Residential Switches" - NEC.
Step 6: Connecting the New Switch
With the wires prepared, connect each wire to the corresponding terminal on the new switch. Be sure to tighten the screws securely to avoid loose connections that could generate heat and pose a risk.
Source: "Secure Connection Techniques for Switches" - ESFI.
Step 7 – Installing the New Switch in the Box

Make sure to fix the cables in their new position correctly. In Argentina, the colors black, brown or gray indicate the phase; while the neutral is blue; On the other hand, the ground wire is usually two-color, green and yellow.
Place the new switch in the box and screw it in tightly. Make sure it is level and flush with the wall. Replace the switch plate and tighten the screws.
Source: "Procedures for Safe Installation of Switches" - OSHA.
Step 8: Power Restoration

Once the new switch is installed correctly, restore power to the electrical panel. Verify switch operation by testing connected lights or other devices. If everything works as it should, you have successfully completed the installation!

This tutorial provides a step-by-step guide for beginners in installing electrical switches. Always remember to follow safety regulations and, if you have any questions, seek the guidance of an electrical professional.

Note: This tutorial is informational and is not a substitute for guidance from a certified electrical professional. Always check local electrical codes and regulations before performing any electrical work.

title: First aid in electrical incidents: crucial answers
excerpt: The ability to provide first aid in electrical incident situations is crucial to mitigating damage and saving lives. Here are essential guidelines for immediate responses in the event of an accident

blocks.text: The ability to provide first aid in electrical incident situations is crucial to mitigating damage and saving lives. Here are essential guidelines for immediate responses in the event of electrical accidents:
1. Personal safety first:
Before approaching the victim, make sure the environment is safe. Turn off the electricity source if possible and wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) before approaching.
2. Emergency call:
Seek medical help immediately. Call the local emergency number and provide accurate information about the situation, including possible electrocution.
3. Do not touch the victim directly:

Avoid directly touching the victim if they are still in contact with the electrical current. Use non-conductive materials, such as wood, rubber, or even cloth clothing to move the person away from the electrical source.
4. Checking vital signs:

Check the victim's breathing and pulse. Start the cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) if necessary and trained to do so. Different government and private organizations offer free resuscitation and first aid courses.
5. Don't use water:
Avoid using water to treat electrical burns. Instead, cover them with a sterile dressing and seek medical attention.
6. Keep curious people away:
Keep other people away from the area to avoid further accidents. Establish a secure perimeter until professional help arrives.
7. Assess possible injuries:
Check the victim for possible additional injuries, such as fractures or damage to the spine. Take necessary actions with caution.
8. Provide comfort and calm:
Keep the victim calm. Provide comfort and emotional support while waiting for emergency professionals to arrive.
Sources on first aid for electrical accidents:
American Red Cross : First Aid/CPR/AED.
National Fire Protection Association (NFPA): Electrical Safety.

The ability to act quickly and effectively in electrical emergency situations can make the difference between complete recovery and complications. Training in specific first aid for electrical incidents is essential for any professional in this field.

title: Understanding the relationship between current and voltage
excerpt: What is the best way to understand the relationship between current and voltage

blocks.text: In the world of electricity, understanding the relationship between current and voltage is essential for any professional. In this article we will break down the basic concepts that make up this very important link.
Electric current:

Electric current, measured in amperes (A), represents the flow of electrical charge through a conductor. It is essentially the number of electrons that circulate per unit of time. The higher the current, the more electrons are moving.
Voltage or tension:

Voltage, measured in volts (V), refers to the force that drives current through a circuit. It is the difference in electrical potential between two points and determines the amount of energy per unit charge.
Resistance:
Resistance in an electrical circuit hinders the flow of current. It is measured in ohms and is crucial in controlling the amount of current that can flow in a given circuit.
Ohm's Law Relationship:
The basic relationship between current, voltage and resistance is governed by Ohm's Law: V = I x R , where V is the voltage, I is the current and R is the resistance in ohms (Ω).
Electrical power:

Power, measured in watts (W), is the amount of energy transferred per unit of time. It is related to current and voltage by the formula: P = I x v. Controlling power is vital to ensure efficient and safe performance of electrical devices.
Practical applications:

Understanding these basic relationships is crucial to design, maintain and troubleshoot electrical systems. From home lighting to industrial machinery, understanding how current and voltage interact with each other is key.
Sources:
"Introduction to Electric Circuits" - James A. Svoboda, Richard C. Dorf.
"Electric Circuits" - Nilsson & Riedel.
IEEE Transactions on Power Systems.
Through this fundamental understanding, electrical professionals can effectively address challenges in various environments, ensuring safe and efficient use of electrical energy.

title: Proper use of Personal Protective Equipment
excerpt: The best use of PPE personal protective equipment to avoid risks and dangers for electricians

blocks.text: Safety at work is of utmost importance, especially for those who work in the electrical sector. Professional electricians face risks inherent in their daily work, and the proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is crucial to guarantee a safe and prevent possible accidents . Here are some essential tips for electricians regarding the use of PPE.
1. Know and understand your PPE:
Before starting any work, familiarize yourself with the type of PPE required for specific task . Understand its function, how it should be used and when it needs to be replaced.
2. Wear safety clothing:

Safety clothing, such as flame-resistant and insulated coveralls, is essential to protect against potential arc flash and hazardous materials. Likewise, the Clothing must be comfortable and comply with safety regulations .
3. Protect your eyes and face:
The use of safety glasses and face shields is crucial to prevent eye injuries caused by particles, sparks or other electrical hazards.
4. Insulating gloves:

Wear appropriate insulating gloves to protect against electrical shock. Check its integrity before each use and replace them if they show signs of wear. Remember that there is a classification, according to the maximum tension they can withstand. The classes are the following:

items: Class 00: up to 500 volts
Class 0: up to 1,000 volts
Class 1: up to 7,500 volts
Class 2: up to 17,000 volts
Class 3: up to 26,500 volts

blocks.text: 5. Safety footwear:

Opt for shoes with non-slip and electricity-resistant soles. This will provide an additional layer of protection and will prevent possible injuries caused by electrical currents . Remember that all elements must comply with the corresponding standards.
6. Protective helmets:
In situations where there is risk of falling objects or impacts, the use of protective helmets is essential . Make sure they are properly adjusted and in good condition.
7. Safety Harness
If the task is to be executed in levels from 2 meters high With respect to the lower horizontal plane closest or superior to it, a fall prevention system must be used.
The harness is a device for securing the operator's body to an anchor point intended to stop falls at different levels and prevent severe damage.

The anchor point must be located at the same level as or above the user's waist. Always select anchors whose resistance is not less than 1,500 kg . Discard all those structures of doubtful resistance.
Always keep at least one lanyard connected to its useful anchor point for the duration of the operation at height. The mooring used must comply with regulations and have an energy absorption system.

Before starting the task, verify, through a checklist, the general condition of the harness, observing the most important points such as textile bands, seams, metal buckles, carabiners and most importantly, the fall absorber.
(Resolution 61/2023 of the Superintendence of Occupational Risks)
8. Keep your PPE in good condition:
Perform regular inspections of your equipment . Replace any damaged or worn items to ensure continued effectiveness.
9. Continuous training:
Participate in training programs on electrical safety and the correct use of PPE. Stay updated on the latest regulations and best practices.
10. Report Problems:
If you find any problems with your PPE, report it immediately. N or compromise your safety or that of your co-workers .

Remembering these tips and applying them in the work environment will significantly contribute to the safety and well-being of professional electricians. Prioritizing safety is not only an individual responsibility, but also a fundamental requirement for a workplace. efficient work and without incident .

title: Principles of electrical resistance: simplified concepts
excerpt: Discover the principles of electrical resistance to apply the fundamental laws in your electrical work.

blocks.text: Electrical resistance is a fundamental concept in the world of electricity, crucial to understanding how materials interact with current flow. We break down the essential principles of this phenomenon in a simple way.
1. Definition:

Electrical resistance, measured in ohms (Ω), is the difficulty electrons encounter in moving through a conductor. In simple terms, it is the opposition that a material presents to the passage of electric current.
2. Ohm's Law:

Ohm's Law establishes the relationship between voltage (V), current (I) and resistance ® in a circuit. The fundamental formula is V = I x R , where the voltage is equal to the product of the current and the resistance.
3. Factors affecting resistance:
Conductive material: Each material has a specific resistivity that determines its ability to resist the flow of electrons.
Conductor length: The longer the conductor, the greater the resistance as the electrons face greater opposition.
Cross-sectional area: A larger cross-section reduces resistance by providing more space for electrons to move.
4. Resistance in series and parallel:
Series: The total resistance in a series circuit is the sum of the individual resistances.
Parallel: The total resistance in a parallel circuit is inversely proportional to the inverse sum of the individual resistances.
5. Power and energy in resistances:
The power dissipated in a resistor is calculated by P = I2 x R or V2/R
The energy consumed by a resistor is calculated by E = P x t , where t It's time.
6. Practical applications:
Electronics: determines the efficiency of electrical components.
Industry : controls the amount of heat generated by electrical equipment.
Lighting : defines the luminosity of the lamps based on the resistance.
7. Sources:
"Principles of Electrical Resistance" - James A. Svoboda, Richard C. Dorf.
"Fundamentals of Electric Circuits" - Charles K. Alexander, Matthew N. O. Sadiku.
IEEE Transactions on Power Systems.

title: Cable channeling in industries: types, benefits and key aspects
excerpt: Learn about the importance of cable channeling in industries, its benefits, the main types of channeling and the regulatory aspects to take into account.

blocks.text: The industrial electrical conduit It is part of the infrastructure that allows the conductors to be protected, organized and maintained throughout the entire installation. Its design and assembly must take into account the characteristics of the production process, the environmental conditions, the equipment involved and the current and future needs of the plant.
A correctly executed pipeline facilitates maintenance, improves the organization of the lines and contributes to reducing risks during the operation of the installation.
What is an industrial electrical conduit?
The system used to conduct, support and protect electrical conductors is called channeling.
In industrial environments it can be made up of cable trays, ladders, pipes, tubes, channels, accessories and support systems, among other solutions.

The choice does not depend only on the number of cables. Factors such as circuit voltage, environmental conditions, mechanical stress, temperature, the possibility of corrosion, the type of industrial process and maintenance requirements must also be analyzed.
Therefore, An industrial pipeline must be thought of as part of the electrical design of the installation .
Why is cable routing important in industries?
Industrial facilities usually bring together a large number of circuits in spaces where there are also machines, structures, pipes, production systems and personnel circulation.
In this context, a disorganized or insufficiently protected line can make maintenance tasks difficult and increase drivers' exposure to damage.
A correctly designed pipeline allows:

items: protect cables against certain mechanical stresses;
maintain orderly routes;
facilitate circuit identification;
improve access for inspection and maintenance;
organize different types of laying;
foresee future expansions;
make better use of available spaces;
reduce subsequent interventions on the installation.

blocks.text: Channeling, therefore, is not only a matter of visual order. It is a functional part of the electrical installation.
Benefits of a properly designed pipeline
Driver protection
Cables may be exposed to shocks, vibrations, friction, humidity, dust, high temperatures and other factors typical of each industrial environment.
The channeling system must be selected in accordance with these conditions to provide the corresponding protection in each case.
Easier maintenance
Cable routing in industries allows circuits to be located and accessed more easily.
This is especially important in plants where an electrical intervention may require coordinating work with production, mechanical maintenance, security and other areas.
The clearer the distribution is, the easier it is to intervene on it.
Power, control and instrumentation organization
Power, control, instrumentation, communications and other systems cables can coexist in a plant.
Planning the routes allows you to establish an adequate distribution and consider the necessary separations to avoid operating problems and interference.
Greater ability to adapt
Industrial facilities change.
Machines are incorporated, processes are modified, sensors are added, production lines are expanded or equipment is replaced.
A pipeline that considers available capacity and future routes can facilitate these modifications and avoid unnecessarily complex work.
Better use of infrastructure
The design of the routes allows you to take advantage of available spaces and previously define support points, intersections and accesses.
This is particularly relevant in existing facilities, where the available space is usually limited by other structures and services.
What should be taken into account when designing an industrial pipeline?
There is no single pipeline system suitable for all industries.
Before defining a solution, it is necessary to analyze the particular characteristics of the project.
Circuit type
A power cable does not require the same treatment as one intended for instrumentation, control or communications.
The nature of the circuits must be considered from the route planning stage.
Quantity and characteristics of cables
The diameter, weight, quantity and arrangement of the conductors directly influence the selection and sizing of the pipeline.
The thermal conditions associated with the concentration of cables must also be considered.
Environmental conditions
The presence of moisture, dust, chemicals, corrosive agents, high temperatures or exposure to the elements can completely modify the appropriate solution.
mechanical stress
In an industrial plant there may be traffic of vehicles, machinery, vibrations, accidental impacts and other factors that must be considered when defining the protection and support of the lines.
Support system
It is not enough to select a tray or a pipe.
It is also necessary to determine how it will be supported, where the supports will be located and what loads it will have to support.
A correctly installed pipeline requires a support structure in accordance with the conditions of the project.
Maintenance and expansions
The route must allow inspections and subsequent work to be carried out without turning each intervention into a work.
It is also advisable to consider from the beginning the possibility of incorporating new circuits.
Types of piping used in industrial facilities
The solution depends on the characteristics of each project. Among the most frequently used systems are:
Cable trays
The trays allow large quantities of cables to be distributed through organized and accessible routes.
There are different configurations, including perforated trays and ladder trays.
They are common in industrial plants because they allow extensive cables to be organized and facilitate certain inspection, maintenance and expansion tasks.
Its selection must consider, among other factors, the cable load, materials, environmental conditions and the support system.
Cable ladders
Ladders use stringers and crossbars to support the cables.
Its configuration allows good accessibility and is appropriate for certain power and industrial distribution lines.
Pipes and tubes
Tubes and pipes can provide physical protection to conductors and allow routes where a more closed system is required.
Metallic or non-metallic, rigid or flexible solutions can be used, depending on the characteristics of the installation.
Channels and closed pipelines
Closed systems allow conductors to be contained and provide additional protection against certain external conditions.
The choice depends on the environment, the circuits involved and the construction characteristics of the installation.
Channeling in special industrial environments
Some facilities present conditions that require a particular analysis.

In sectors with the presence of corrosive substances, combustible dust, flammable gases or vapors, for example, the selection of materials and piping systems must be made taking into account the specific conditions of the area.
Classified areas
In installations where an explosive atmosphere may exist, it is not enough to select a conventional tray or pipe.
The classification of the area and the particular conditions of the installation must first be determined.

The regulations AEA IEC 60079-10-1 and AEA IEC 60079-10-2 , in their current editions, respectively contemplate the classification of areas where explosive atmospheres may exist due to gases, vapors or mists, and due to combustible dust.
In these cases, the channeling must be part of a comprehensive solution compatible with the equipment, accessories, enclosures and protection systems used.
Regulations applicable in Argentina
The regulations related to industrial electrical installations are not reduced to a single standard.
The applicable regulations depend on the characteristics of the project, the level of tension, the type of establishment, the environment and the activity carried out.
Among the references that should be considered are:
Law 19,587 on Hygiene and Safety at Work
Establishes the general hygiene and safety framework applicable to work establishments in Argentina.
Decree 351/79
It regulates Law 19,587 and its Annex VI contains the Chapter 14 – Electrical Installations .
There are requirements related to electrical installations, conductors, conduits, grounding and protection against direct and indirect contacts, among other aspects.

The Decree also establishes the need to consider the corresponding regulations of the Argentine Electrotechnical Association and that the materials and equipment used respond to applicable national or international standards.
AEA Regulations
The regulations of the Argentine Electrotechnical Association (AEA) They constitute a fundamental technical reference for the design and execution of electrical installations.
Within them is the family AEA 90364 , corresponding to low voltage electrical installations.

However, it should not be interpreted that there is a single regulation applicable to any industrial pipeline. The corresponding standard or normative part must be determined according to the characteristics of each installation.
IRAM and IEC standards
The standards corresponding to the products and systems used must also be considered.
The family IRAM 62386 , for example, contemplates tube and accessory systems for low-voltage electrical installations.
For cable tray and ladder systems, IEC 61537 constitutes a specific international reference for these systems.
In areas with risk of explosion, family rules are also relevant. IEC 60079 , adopted in Argentina through the corresponding regulations and technical standards.
A fundamental consideration: industrial activity
The applicable regulations may also vary depending on the activity.

For example, facilities linked to certain mining activities are covered by specific regulations. In these cases, it is necessary to analyze the regulatory regime corresponding to the establishment before defining the design and execution criteria.
Therefore, Regulatory compliance must be evaluated for each project and not through a generic list of standards applied indiscriminately .
Why hire PyP Electricidad?
Industrial trunking is not simply about installing a tray and placing cables inside.
It requires analyzing the route, the equipment involved, the environmental conditions, the support systems, the distribution of the circuits and the maintenance and expansion needs.
At PyP Electricidad we integrate channeling and laying work within a broader vision of the industrial electrical installation.

Our experience includes electromechanical works, panel integration, automation and maintenance , which allows the cables to be addressed taking into account their relationship with the rest of the installation.
Among the jobs we can carry out are:

items: planning and execution of routes;
installation of cable trays and ladders;
mounting of support systems;
installation of pipes and conduits;
laying and organization of conductors;
integration with electrical panels;
identification and organization of circuits;
intervention on existing facilities;
Work associated with plant expansions and modifications.

blocks.text: Furthermore, PyP Electricidad works under a management system that includes ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 , integrating quality criteria, environmental management and occupational health and safety.
A well-made pipeline starts before the first cable
In an industrial plant, a tray, a ladder or a pipe may seem secondary elements compared to a panel, a motor or a production line.
But they are part of the infrastructure that allows all these devices to be connected.
A good pipeline must respond to the present of the installation, but also consider its maintenance, its operating conditions and the modifications that may arise over time.
Therefore, Cable routing is also part of the electrical engineering of an industrial plant .

title: Residential Panelboard Inspection: A Practical Guide for New Electricians
excerpt: Summary for inspection of home electrical panels - panel inspection guide

blocks.text: <strong class="text-brand-light"> Electrical panel (image from Freepik)

Regular maintenance of electrical panels is essential to ensure the safe and efficient operation of the electrical system of a building or home. In this tutorial, we'll explore the key strategies for carrying out effective dashboard maintenance.
Step 1: visual inspection

It begins with a detailed visual inspection of the entire electrical panel. Look for signs of wear, damage, loose connections, or dust buildup. Identifying problems visually is the first step to preventing possible failures.
Source: "Visual Inspection Guide for Electrical Panels" - National Fire Protection Association (NFPA).
Step 2: Check connections
Make sure all connections are tight and in good condition. Loose connections can generate heat and pose a fire hazard. Tighten any loose screws or terminals and check the integrity of the cables.
Source: "Connection verification procedures for electrical panels" - Electrical Safety Foundation International (ESFI).
Step 3: Functional Testing

Perform functional tests on each switch, circuit breaker and protective device. Verify that all switches operate correctly and that protective devices respond appropriately to short circuits and overloads.
Source: "Test Procedures for Protective Equipment" - NFPA 70B.
Step 4: Cleaning the board
Clean the electrical panel regularly to remove accumulated dust and dirt. Use a dry cloth and avoid using abrasive chemicals. Proper cleaning helps prevent short circuits.
Source: "Preventive maintenance: cleaning electrical panels" - Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE).
Step 5: Clear and precise labeling
Make sure all circuits are clearly and accurately labeled. Proper labeling facilitates quick identification during inspections and maintenance, which will save time and reduce potential errors.
Source: "The importance of labeling on electrical panels" - NFPA 70E.
Step 6: Continuous Monitoring

Implement a continuous monitoring system to alert you of potential problems. Modern monitoring devices can detect changes in temperature, current and voltage, allowing preventive interventions before serious problems occur.
Source: "Advantages of continuous monitoring in electrical panels" - Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI).
Step 7: Staff training
Make sure maintenance staff are properly trained. Provides training on safety and maintenance procedures specific to the electrical panel. Trained personnel is key to effective maintenance.
Source: "The Importance of Electrical Maintenance Training" - Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA).
Personnel must be sufficiently trained to carry out all necessary tasks that requires assigned work .
Source: ISO 45001 STANDARD – Clause 7-SUPPORT: 7.2 Competence 7.3 Awareness.

Note: This tutorial is informational and is not a substitute for the guidance of a certified electrical professional. Always check local electrical codes and regulations before performing any electrical work.

title: Safe Electrical Connections – Detailed Tutorial
excerpt: Know what you need to make safe electrical connections. We offer you a step-by-step tutorial for beginners.

blocks.text: <strong class="text-brand-light"> Image by Freepick

Making safe electrical connections is vital to guarantee the proper functioning of the installation in the home or in any building. Below we provide you with a brief step-by-step summary of how to make a safe electrical connection:

Important: Before starting any electrical work, ensure that the power supply is disconnected from the main panel. If you do not feel comfortable performing these steps, seek the help of a qualified professional. Safety comes first.
Materials and tools necessary to make safe electrical connections:

items: Insulated screwdriver: Use an insulated screwdriver to avoid possible electrical shock. Make sure it is in good condition before use.

Wire stripper: Use the wire stripper to remove approximately 1 cm of the insulating coating from the ends of the cables you are connecting. Adjust the tool so that it does not cut the internal conductors.

Connection terminals suitable for wire gauge: Select terminals that suit the gauge of your cables. If necessary, follow the manufacturer's instructions to install them correctly. You can get the exact terminals for your project in our online store .
Needle nose pliers: Use needle nose pliers to bend and adjust the wires as needed during the connection process.
Insulating tape or shrink connectors: Use electrical tape or shrink connectors to insulate the connection and prevent short circuits. Roll the tape several times to ensure good protection.
Multimeter (optional, but recommended to check connection): A multimeter is useful to check for voltage in the wires before you start and to make sure the connection is solid after you make it.

blocks.text: Steps to make general home electrical connections:

items: Disconnecting power supply : Turn off the switch or disable the corresponding switch on the main board.
Cable detection : Identify the cables you are going to connect. Make sure there is no current in them using a voltage tester, pole finder, or multimeter.
Stripping the ends of the cables - Use the wire stripper to remove approximately 1cm of insulating coating from the ends of the cables you are connecting.
Preparation of the terminals : If you are using connection terminals, install them on the stripped ends of the wires following the manufacturer's instructions.
Cable connection : Connect the cables making sure they are tight. If you are using a screw connector, tighten it properly.
Connection isolation - Use electrical tape or shrink connectors to insulate the connection and prevent short circuits or wire exposure.
V verification with a multimeter (optional) - If you have access to a multimeter, check the connection to ensure there are no shorts and that the installation is solid.
Reactivation of the power supply - Once you make sure everything is properly connected and insulated, turn the power back on.

blocks.text: Additional tips for a home electrical connection:

items: Always follow local rules and regulations.
If you are unsure, seek the help of an electrical professional.
Do not overload the circuits and use quality materials.
Maintain a clean and tidy work area.

Remember, Safety is the most important thing when working with electricity . It is always advisable to consult a professional electrician for more complex tasks or if you have doubts about the safety of an electrical connection.

title: The secret of how to choose the right light temperature 💡
excerpt: Lamps are not only an object that serves to illuminate, they also help to create environments, highlight objects and textures, and with their light they influence people's mood. Like sunlight, which changes color.

blocks.text: <strong class="text-brand-light"> Image from Freepik
Lamps are not only an object that serves to illuminate, they also help create environments, highlight objects and textures, and with their light they influence people's mood.

Like sunlight, which changes color throughout the day, LED lamps, in their different versions, come in various color temperatures, which is measured in degrees Kelvin (K). The higher this value, the cooler the color will be.

During the morning and midday, natural light tends to be colder, with bluish tones. This is because sunlight passes through more of the atmosphere before reaching the earth, filtering out the warmer wavelengths and leaving the colder wavelengths predominant. This type of cold light is ideal for waking up, concentrating and performing active tasks.

In the afternoon, the sunlight begins to soften and take on warmer, golden tones. The light temperature gradually decreases, creating a feeling of warmth and comfort. This warm light is perfect for relaxing, clearing your mind and preparing for rest.

Cold light is light that has a high color temperature, between 5000 K and 6500 K. Its tone is bluish or pure white, and resembles the light of midday or a clear sky. Cold light is very bright and sharp, and allows you to see colors more faithfully. Lamps of these temperatures also help to create more modern and minimalist environments, since they highlight geometric shapes and contrasts.

On the other hand, warm light is light that has a low color temperature, between 2700 K and 3000 K. Its tone is yellowish or orange, and resembles the light of dawn or dusk. Warm light is softer and more welcoming, and creates more diffuse shadows. Likewise, it helps create more classic and rustic environments, as it highlights warm colors and natural textures.

title: ISO 45001 standards: what every electrician should know
excerpt: List of safety recommendations according to ISO 45001 standards

blocks.text: <strong class="text-brand-light"> Image from Freepik

The ISO:45001 standard is an international standard for the certification of Occupational Health and Safety Management. In this framework, it is important that electricians are aware of occupational health and safety regulations to guarantee a work environment with risks reduced as much as possible. Here are some key practices every electrician should know:
Risk assessment:
Before starting any electrical task, carry out a risk assessment. Identify potential hazards, such as frayed cables, faulty equipment, or adverse environmental conditions.
Training of personnel in ISO 45001 standards:
Make sure your colleagues are properly trained in electrical safety. Provides information to keep everyone aware of best security practices and procedures.
Use of safe equipment and tools:
Use only certified electrical equipment and tools in good condition. Regularly inspect cables and plugs for damage and replace them if necessary.
Labeling and blocking:
Clearly label switches and electrical panels . Implements lockout procedures to ensure equipment is secure during maintenance or repair work.
Preventive maintenance:
Schedule regular maintenance for electrical equipment and systems. This includes inspecting cables, connections, and cleaning any dust and debris that may affect performance.
Personal protection:
Promotes the proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), such as insulated gloves, safety glasses and helmets. These elements are essential to reduce the risk of injury.
Signage:
Install clear, visible signage to indicate electrical hazard areas. This will alert others to possible risks and encourage caution.
Emergency protocols:
Establish clear emergency protocols in case of electrical accidents. Ensure that all staff are aware of emergency procedures and that regular drills are conducted.
Sources:
https://safetyculture.com/es/temas/iso-45001/
https://www.oitcinterfor.org/sites/default/files/preve_electrica.pdf

Knowing and complying with these regulations is essential for the safety and well-being of electricians. Additionally, it helps maintain high standards in the electrical industry, ensuring a safe work environment for everyone.

title: How to perform an electrical safety inspection step by step
excerpt: Learn how to perform an electrical inspection correctly. Perform an inspection like a professional.

blocks.text: <strong class="text-brand-light"> Image from Freepik
Performing an electrical safety inspection is essential to prevent risks and ensure a safe work environment. Here is a step-by-step guide to carry out this inspection:
Planning and preparation before electrical inspection
Identify all areas that will be inspected.
Make sure you have the necessary tools and safety equipment, such as dielectric gloves, protective glasses, and insulated tools.
Documentation review
Examine electrical plans to understand power distribution.
Check documentation for previous maintenance and repairs.
Visual inspection
Look for signs of wear, damage, or overheating on cables and connections.
Examine electrical panels for loose wires or faulty connections.
Verification of protection devices
Make sure all switches, fuses and circuit breakers are in good working order.
Check the presence and accessibility of fire extinguishers and first aid equipment.
Functional tests
Performs functional tests on emergency switches, exit lights and alarm systems.
Verify the operation of the emergency disconnect devices.
Grounding systems
Confirms that grounding systems are properly installed and connected.
Perform continuity tests on ground conductors.
Lighting
Make sure all areas are adequately lit.
Replace faulty lamps and clean fixtures if necessary.
Signage
Verify correct signage of electrical danger areas.
Inspect warning labels and safety procedures.
Record of results
Documents all findings and necessary corrective actions.
Establish an action plan to address any identified issues.
Training and communication
Provide training to your employees or colleagues on electrical hazards and safety measures.
Communicate inspection results and actions taken.
Remember that electrical safety is an ongoing effort and must be integrated into the work culture.
